public_health_question.v: How did the proportions of circulating SARS-CoV-2 Omicron lineages change in the United States during January 2022–May 2023?

ev.q: This report summarizes U.S. trends in variant proportions from national genomic surveillance during January 2022–May 2023.
Genomic Surveillance for SARS-CoV-2 Variants: Circulation of Omicron Lineages
This report summarizes U.S. trends in variant proportions from national genomic surveillance
CDC’s national genomic surveillance system integrates SARS-CoV-2 sequences from three sources
public sequence data repositories, including the Global Initiative on Sharing All Influenza Data (GISAID) repository
the National SARS-CoV-2 Strain Surveillance (NS3) program
Global Initiative on Sharing All Influenza Data (GISAID) repository
National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) GenBank
positive nucleic acid amplification tests from COVID-19 electronic laboratory reporting (CELR)
regional-level data from the National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System (NREVSS)
Weekly variant proportions were estimated at the national and U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) regional levels

equity.level_reason: No social-position dimension; comparisons are across lineages, weeks and HHS regions.

notes: Variant-attributed cases are NAAT counts multiplied by proportions (arithmetic). The methods comparison (CELR vs NREVSS weights) is recorded as a sensitivity analysis; it is a consistency check of the estimator, not of a contrast.
